text:
Mira Chen: Quick heads-up — I'm starting a living doc for the long-range platform roadmap focused on routing policies, multi-region, and multi-tenant isolation. Need product + eng alignment on launch criteria and priority customers.
Jordan Patel: Great — can you include margins for cost vs latency tradeoffs? customers keep asking for predictable unit economics.
Mira Chen: Yes. Plan is sections: customer asks, launch criteria, minimal viable policy set, migration path, and metrics to validate.
Alex Rivera: From infra side: we need concrete constraints for cross-region failover and a safe default routing policy that degrades gracefully.
Samir Gupta: Agree. Also add a compatibility matrix for model variants (quantized vs fp16) + routing fallback rules.
Priya Nair: Customer asks we've heard: 1) region pinning for data residency, 2) SLA-backed latency for priority tenants, 3) clear isolation lanes for compliance customers.
Mira Chen: Noted. For launch criteria I'm proposing: (a) canonical policy templates (region-pin, cost-preferred, low-latency), (b) telemetry for per-tenant tail latency, (c) rollback policy and automated fallback to lower-capacity model variants. Thoughts?
Jordan Patel: That makes sense. Add acceptance tests: synthetic latency/regression tests + 2 pilot customers on Dedicated.
Alex Rivera: Ops constraints: autoscaling interactions. Need documented SLOs for burst behavior and a mechanism to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbor storms.
Samir Gupta: Can we define a hard isolation mode (no cross-tenant routing, no cache sharing) vs soft isolation (best-effort affinity + shared infra)? Put migration path between them.
Mira Chen: Yes — draft will call them "Isolated" and "Affinity-optimized" lanes, with explicit tradeoffs/cost multipliers.
Priya Nair: Sales ask: pricing anchors for isolation lanes. If isolation costs 2x, we need customer-facing justification (audit logs, KMS, support).
Jordan Patel: We'll need a rollout playbook: 1) internal canary, 2) alpha customers, 3) pilot on Dedicated, 4) gradual GA. Each stage has gating criteria (observability, regressions, cost delta).
Mira Chen: On observability gates: token-level cost breakdown, per-route p99, error budgets, and regression on model output quality.
Alex Rivera: Add stress tests for cross-region links and simulated AZ failures. Must validate fallback latency within X ms (TBD).
Samir Gupta: For policy arbitration: propose priority order: tenant affinity > region constraint (if explicit) > cost preference. Document edge cases where tie-breakers use latency estimates.
Priya Nair: Customer negotiation note: some enterprise customers will demand hard region isolation + storage residency; we should surface a delivery timeline and required procurement.
Mira Chen: Action items: I'll create PR for the living doc, include a proposed default policy template and the isolation lane definitions. @Jordan can you draft the acceptance test list? @Alex + @Samir please add ops constraints and fallback SLAs.
Jordan Patel: On it. I'll sketch test matrix and milestone estimates.
Alex Rivera: I'll add autoscaler and stress-test requirements.
Samir Gupta: I'll author the compatibility matrix for model variants and fallback sequencing.
Priya Nair: I'll gather the top 3 enterprise asks and price-sensitivity notes.
ProductBot: Reminder: create RFC by EOD Friday — label: roadmap/routing-isolation.
Mira Chen: Thanks — aiming to have initial RFC + policy templates by next Wed. If anyone has customer examples or specific metrics to include, paste them here. :sparkles:
Jordan Patel: I'll drop the pilot test script and sample telemetry configs to the doc once initial PR is up.
Mira Chen: Perfect. Closing thread for now — will ping when RFC is ready for review. :rocket:
